videos.title: The Hidden Danger Inside Every Candle
videos.point: Paraffin wax vapor autoignites at ~225°C once boiling (~370°C) because oxygen mixes at the top, and water on superheated wax triggers steam explosions that launch fireballs.
content: Autoignition temperature of wax vapor lower than boiling point
Hairline cracks in containers leak jets that flash-boil water
Fire starts at the top where vapor meets oxygen, not at water contact
Pouring water on a burning candle can create a fireball
videos.watch_why: Physics of autoignition and steam expansion explain the danger; replaces the experiment footage.
